# Implementation Plan: crews v3.6.0 — lead-side review-mail exact-duplicate collapse (D-001)

*Generated by `/plan-with-ralph` on 2026-06-04. Ready for `/implement-with-ralph --from-plan .ralph/jobs/crews-redundant-empty-kind-tag-emissions/plan.md`.*

## Overview

This plan ships D-001 from the brainstorm `.ralph/brainstorms/crews-redundant-empty-kind-tag-emissions/selected-direction.md` — a lead-side display-only collapse of consecutive same-`(sender, kind, body-hash, summary)` rows in `/crews:review-mail`, with empty `replyTo` / `acks` / `decisions` metadata. The durable outbox.jsonl / mailbox-history.jsonl audit log is untouched. Each collapsed group emits one stderr warning (when `count >= warnThreshold`) plus one `crews.log` line (always). The review cursor advances past all collapsed rows as if individually reviewed. Env switches `CREWS_REVIEW_MAIL_COLLAPSE=off` (disable) and `CREWS_REVIEW_MAIL_COLLAPSE_WARN_THRESHOLD=<N>` (default 3) are operator escape hatches. D-002 telemetry (per-collapse log line carrying memberName/crew/kind/count/seqRange/bodyHashPrefix/version) is bundled into the same per-collapse log entry, so this single ship reduces lead-side review noise AND produces the grep-able classification signal Devil's Advocate asked for.

Ships as crews **v3.6.0** in the `ai-developer-toolkit` submodule. Per `AGENTS.md` worktree convention this lands inside that submodule (`ai-developer-toolkit/.worktrees/<task-id>/`), followed by a codexu-side submodule-pointer-bump commit.

## Research Findings

### Codebase Context

Crews is a Node/CommonJS plugin at `ai-developer-toolkit/plugins/crews/` (in-tree submodule). Deployed version: **3.5.0**. The lead's review surface is `hooks/commands/review-mail.js` (282 lines), the durable audit log is written by `hooks/stop.js::appendOutboxBatch` (no changes here), and there is already a discriminated-result body-resolution helper at `hooks/resolve-body.js`. Tests run via `node tests/run.js` (one Worker per file, ~60s target on Windows at default concurrency 10). The deployed test surface includes `tests/review-mail-command.test.js`, `tests/strict-ack-review-mail.test.js`, and `tests/command-args-parity.test.js` — the last one pins stdout key order at lines `191-196` and must be updated when the JSON shape is extended.

- Seeded from brainstorm: `.ralph/brainstorms/crews-redundant-empty-kind-tag-emissions/selected-direction.md`
- Validated brainstorm line refs against v3.5.0 (most still accurate; deltas captured in `research-brief.md`)

### Technical Constraints

- **Body-hash source**: must hash `bodyText(row)` (the pre-fallback delivered body at `review-mail.js:91-97`) NOT the resolved-from-id cross-read body. The brainstorm called this out and the architect + Codex confirmed it.
- **No normalized boolean env parser**: existing pattern is inline `String(env).trim().toLowerCase() !== 'off'` (e.g. `CREWS_BODY_CANONICAL` at `stop.js:158-160`). New env switches follow this convention.
- **No runtime plugin-version reader exists**: must add a tiny `lib/version.js` helper that reads `.claude-plugin/plugin.json` via `getPluginRoot()` from `hooks/paths.js:50`. Tests already read the manifest directly in `tests/version.test.js`.
- **`appendLog(line, cwd)` signature**: single-line string + state-cwd; stamps `[ISO] ${line}`; convention is grep-able key=value text, not JSON. Failure is silent. Existing log lines (e.g. `review-mail: bodyResolution=... for memberName=... outboxSeq=...`) define the line shape.
- **CLI stderr warnings**: `runCliCommand()` only writes stdout via `formatSuccess`. Per-collapse stderr requires explicit `process.stderr.write()` inside the handler (bypassing the formatSuccess contract). The slash form will simply not surface stderr to the operator at all (slash output is folded into the agent transcript); the env-switch `WARN_THRESHOLD=Infinity` is the slash-side opt-out if needed.
- **Empty-metadata predicate**: must check top-level `replyTo`, `payload.replyTo`, legacy `payload.replyToId` (v3.0.0 rename), `acks`, and `decisions`. System-routed envelopes carry their reply-target in `payload.replyToId` historically.
- **Cursor preservation**: `lastReviewedSeq` already computes from `allRows` (un-collapsed) at `review-mail.js:205-209`. The collapse pass operates on the displayed entries only; cursor advancement is structurally preserved. `tests/strict-ack-review-mail.test.js` must pass without modification.
- **Test runner & serial denylist**: `tests/run.js` runs worker-per-file at concurrency 10, with a serial tail for race-sensitive files. New tests should not need denylist entries unless they exercise Windows process/lock timing. Target: < 60s default-concurrency wall time.

## Approach

### Architecture

**Two-layer split (purity + side-effects)** per Phase 4 review F-009:

1. **PURE helper `lib/collapse-review-rows.js`** — `collapseReviewRows(rows)` takes an array of expanded raw rows (output of `rows.flatMap(expandReviewRows)`) and returns
   ```
   {
     collapsedRows: [row, ...],          // head row per group (with _collapsedCount/_collapsedSeqs/_collapsedIds attached when group size > 1)
     collapseGroups: [
       {
         count, seqRange: [a, b], bodyHashPrefix, kind, sender,
         memberSeqs: [seq, ...], memberIds: [id, ...], memberConsumedAts: [iso, ...]
       },
       ...                                 // ONE entry per group of size >= 2 (size 1 groups omitted)
     ]
   }
   ```
   Helper has NO `appendLog`, NO `process.stderr.write`, NO env reads, NO manifest reads. All I/O happens at the review-mail.js call site (point 4 below).

2. **PURE helper `lib/collapse-key.js`** — body-hash function (sha256 hex; CRLF→LF normalization only, no trim), env-switch parser (`parseCollapseEnv()` returning `{ enabled, warnThreshold }`), empty-metadata predicate (`isEmptyMetadata(row)` checks top-level `replyTo`, `payload.replyTo`, `payload.replyToId`, `acks` length, `decisions` length), and the collapse-key tuple builder (`buildCollapseKey(row)` returning a canonical JSON string for `(sender, kind, bodyHash, summary)` when `isEmptyMetadata(row)` is true, or `null` otherwise to signal "do not collapse").

3. **Runtime helper `lib/version.js`** — `getPluginVersion()` reads `.claude-plugin/plugin.json::version` via `getPluginRoot()` from `hooks/paths.js:50`. Cached in module scope (read-once). NO `package.json` is used — crews has none.

4. **Wire-in at `review-mail.js:199`** — between `const rows = ...` (line 195) and the formatter pass (line 199). All side effects live HERE, not in the helper:
   ```js
   const expanded = rows.flatMap(row => expandReviewRows(row));
   const env = parseCollapseEnv();
   let collapsedRows = expanded;
   if (env.enabled) {
     const { collapsedRows: cr, collapseGroups } = collapseReviewRows(expanded);
     collapsedRows = cr;
     const manifestForTelemetry = manifest;  // already in scope (read at line 184)
     const pluginVersion = getPluginVersion();
     for (const group of collapseGroups) {
       const listenerExit = manifestForTelemetry.terminationReason
         || manifestForTelemetry.listenerState
         || 'unknown';
       const turnBoundaryCount = new Set(group.memberConsumedAts).size;
       const logLine = `review-mail collapse: name=${group.sender} crew=${actor.crew} kind=${group.kind} count=${group.count} seqRange=${group.seqRange[0]}..${group.seqRange[1]} bodyHash=${group.bodyHashPrefix} version=${pluginVersion} listenerExit=${listenerExit} turnBoundaryCount=${turnBoundaryCount}`;
       appendLog(logLine, actor.stateCwd);
       if (args.output === 'cli' && group.count >= env.warnThreshold) {
         process.stderr.write(`crews review-mail: collapsed ${group.count} consecutive same-(sender=${group.sender}, kind=${group.kind}) rows; seqRange=${group.seqRange[0]}..${group.seqRange[1]}; bodyHash=${group.bodyHashPrefix} (use CREWS_REVIEW_MAIL_COLLAPSE=off to disable)\n`);
       }
     }
   }
   const entries = collapsedRows.map(row => formatReviewMailEntry(row, { crew: actor.crew, stateCwd: actor.stateCwd }));
   ```
   `formatReviewMailEntry` is extended to detect attached `_collapsedSeqs[]` / `_collapsedIds[]` / `_collapsedCount` on the input row and surface them in its return as `collapsedSeqs[] / collapsedIds[] / collapsedCount`. For non-collapsed rows (size 1 groups, where the head row has no `_collapsed*` markers), the `collapsed*` fields are ABSENT (preserves pre-3.6.0 JSON shape).

5. **`collapsedIds[]` leaf-id chain** (per F-006): each member id is computed via the chain `row.reportId || row.outboxId || row.id`. This gives drill-down access whether the row is a direct send (parent inbox `id`) or a `payload.entries[]` expansion (leaf `reportId`/`outboxId`).

6. **Cursor invariant**: leave `review-mail.js:205-209` byte-identical. Cursor advancement operates on `allRows` (not `entries` / not `collapsedRows`) so collapse cannot affect `lastReviewedSeq` / `lastReviewedAt`.

7. **Env-switch precedence**: `CREWS_REVIEW_MAIL_COLLAPSE=off` (case-insensitive, leading/trailing whitespace trimmed) short-circuits the collapse pass — `env.enabled === false` skips the whole collapsed-block above so the output is bit-identical to pre-3.6.0 behavior. `CREWS_REVIEW_MAIL_COLLAPSE_WARN_THRESHOLD=<N>` (positive integer; defaults to 3; invalid values fall back to 3 via the existing `readEnvPositiveInt()` helper in `hooks/safe-io.js:60-67`) controls the stderr-warning threshold.

8. **Slash-vs-CLI stderr asymmetry**: the stderr write is gated on `args.output === 'cli'`. Slash invocations (`/crews:review-mail`) set `args.output === 'slash'` and emit only the `crews.log` line; the operator sees collapse evidence via grep, not stderr. CLI invocations (`node tools/crews.js review-mail ...`) emit BOTH the log line AND the stderr warning when threshold is met. AGENTS.md documents this asymmetry (US-011).

9. **D-002 telemetry data sources** (per F-003): `listenerExit` reads `manifest.terminationReason || manifest.listenerState || 'unknown'`. v1.9.0+ manifests have `terminationReason` (`'hard'`/`'soft'`/etc); v3.5.0+ manifests have `listenerState`; pre-v1.9 manifests fall back to `'unknown'`. `turnBoundaryCount` is computed from `new Set(group.memberConsumedAts).size` — purely derived from the collapse group, no manifest read needed for that field.

### Implementation Strategy

Sequential because every story after foundation-libs touches `review-mail.js` or its test:

1. **Phase 1 (parallel-safe)**: US-001 (HEURISTIC offline measurement, no plugin edits, no dependency on the not-yet-built helper) and US-002+US-003 (foundation libs, disjoint files). US-001 deliberately INLINES its own heuristic key-builder so it can run before `lib/collapse-key.js` exists; US-012b later re-runs the measurement using the real `buildCollapseKey` for faithful comparison.
2. **Phase 2 (serial, gated on US-001 reading)**: US-004 (PURE collapse helper, no I/O), US-005 (wire-in at call site with all side effects HERE), US-006 (cursor preservation regression), US-007 (env-off 4-condition boundary), US-008 (slash-vs-CLI stderr split), US-009 (D-002 telemetry derivation at call site).
3. **Phase 3 (serial after impl)**: US-010 (plugin version bump via `bump-version.js` + codexu-root AGENTS.md row), US-011 (CHANGELOG + plugin AGENTS.md), US-012 (final cross-cluster regression run + US-012b FAITHFUL re-measurement using `lib/collapse-key.js` + dashboard + commit + push).

US-001 is the EARLY gate (heuristic): if measured collapse-reduction over the local corpus is < 5% AND the bundled D-002 telemetry doesn't surface an actionable noise pattern, surface a `kind=question` to the lead before US-002+ ships, asking whether to (a) proceed with D-001 as a structural improvement + telemetry channel, (b) defer D-001 in favor of re-ranking toward D-003/D-004, or (c) widen the corpus measurement to other crews / longer history.

US-012b is the LATE verification (faithful): re-runs the measurement using the real `buildCollapseKey` from `lib/collapse-key.js`. If faithful percent_reduction differs from US-001 heuristic by more than 2 percentage points, US-012b flags the heuristic as inaccurate in the ship report. US-012b also re-asserts the safety floor "zero rows with non-empty metadata get coalesced" using the real helper.

## Scope

### In Scope

(Copied verbatim from `selected-direction.md § In Scope`, with annotations preserved):

- New collapse pass in `hooks/commands/review-mail.js::formatReviewMailEntry` (and the row-expansion site at `review-mail.js:121-135, 193-209`) that walks consumed rows in cursor order, groups consecutive rows with the same `(memberName, kind, body-hash, summary, empty replyTo, empty acks, empty decisions)` tuple, and emits one collapsed display row per group.
- Body-hash computed against the actually delivered body (NOT the resolved-from-id fallback at `review-mail.js:99-118`), to avoid false dedup when distinct rows happen to resolve to the same display string.
- Per-collapse stderr warning when `count >= 3` AND a per-collapse `appendLog` entry to `crews.log` listing `(memberName, crew, kind, count, seqRange, bodyHashPrefix)` for every collapse pass regardless of count, so operators can grep for false positives.
- Env switches: `CREWS_REVIEW_MAIL_COLLAPSE=off` disables the pass entirely; `CREWS_REVIEW_MAIL_COLLAPSE_WARN_THRESHOLD=<N>` overrides the default warn-at-3 stderr threshold.
- JSON output shape extension: collapsed rows include `collapsedCount`, `collapsedSeqs`, and `collapsedIds` so any downstream consumer can drill into the underlying envelopes. Single-row entries keep their existing shape (`collapsedCount` absent or equal to 1).
- Test coverage spanning `tests/review-mail-command.test.js` (collapse pass), `tests/strict-ack-review-mail.test.js` (cursor advancement under collapse — must match pre-collapse behavior bit-for-bit), and `tests/command-args-parity.test.js` (env-switch / CLI parity).
- A pre-ship offline measurement: run the collapse pass over the existing local `.crews/ralph-pipeline/members/*/outbox.jsonl` + `mailbox-history.jsonl` corpus that codex already sampled (1086 rows, 47 exact consecutive same-kind duplicates, 245 stub-like rows), produce a raw-vs-collapsed diff, and verify zero rows with non-empty replyTo/acks/decisions get coalesced. **PLANNER NOTE**: planner-side preliminary measurement (see `research-brief.md`) found only 5 extra-dups in 498 mailbox-history rows under a heuristic key; US-001 re-measures with the actual implementation's key and gates on the result.
- Light D-002 telemetry baked into the same change: each collapse pass also logs the listener-exit reason (when discoverable from the actor's manifest) and the inferred turn-boundary count, so operators can use the collapse log to characterize the residual noise pattern without a separate instrumentation ship.
- Version capture: each `crews.log` collapse entry includes the crews plugin `version` from `package.json` so future evidence can be matched to the deployed code. **PLANNER NOTE**: crews has NO `package.json` — version source is `.claude-plugin/plugin.json` via the new `lib/version.js` helper.

> **Planner clarification (F-012)**: Two anachronisms in the verbatim brainstorm quote above. (1) The "stderr warning when `count >= 3`" requirement applies ONLY to CLI invocations (`node tools/crews.js review-mail ...`); slash invocations (`/crews:review-mail`) emit no stderr — see AC1a/AC1b for the explicit split. (2) The "version from `package.json`" wording is wrong for v3.5.0: crews has no `package.json`. The runtime version source is `.claude-plugin/plugin.json::version` via the new `lib/version.js` helper. Both anachronisms are kept in the verbatim quote to preserve brainstorm-traceability; the implementation MUST follow this clarification, not the verbatim wording.

### Out of Scope

(Copied verbatim from `selected-direction.md § Out of Scope`):

- Source-side Stop-hook suppression (D-003). May be revisited as a follow-up after D-001's telemetry quantifies residual noise; the lenses agreed it should ship dry-run / log-only first if it ships at all.
- First-class `noop` / `ack` kind or extension of the v3.2 member system.notification no-kind exemption (D-004). Highest risk to the kind-tag invariant; defer until D-001's collapse telemetry shows a clear "lastKind=done + zero inbox delta + zero strict-ack-pending" pattern dominates the surviving noise.
- v2 Option D (side-channel listener queue, per `crews/docs/architecture-refactor.md` Cause 5 + the line-450 anti-refactor note). Stays on the 2.0 roadmap. D-001 reduces lead-side review pain but does not eliminate model-operated re-arm turns, listener-exit-as-wakeup forcing a model turn, or duplicate report tags emitted within a single model turn — Option D is orthogonal and remains the right v2 lever.
- Near-similarity (Levenshtein / first-200-chars) body matching. v1.x ships exact-normalized-hash only; near-similarity adds policy complexity the lenses agreed is not safe in a first ship.
- Changes to `outbox.jsonl` / `mailbox-history.jsonl` write paths. The durable audit log is untouched.

## Risk Areas

1. **Cursor off-by-one regression** — `lastReviewedSeq` MUST continue computing from `allRows` (un-collapsed) at `review-mail.js:205-209`. Mitigation: US-006 adds an explicit regression test; `tests/strict-ack-review-mail.test.js` is not modified and acts as a permanent anchor.
2. **JSON output-shape break** — adding `collapsedCount/collapsedSeqs/collapsedIds` extends the stdout contract. `tests/command-args-parity.test.js` pins key order at `191-196`. Mitigation: US-005 updates the parity test in the same commit as the wire-in; new fields are documented in AGENTS.md and CHANGELOG.
3. **Body-resolution-fallback collision** — if the body-hash were computed over the resolved cross-read body, distinct rows could collide when both fall back to the same synthesized header. Mitigation: hash MUST be over `bodyText(row)` (pre-fallback), enforced by US-004 unit tests.
4. **Empty-metadata predicate misses `payload.replyToId`** — legacy v3.0.0 field name still appears in older histories. Mitigation: US-003's `isEmptyMetadata(row)` helper checks all five fields (top-level `replyTo`, `payload.replyTo`, `payload.replyToId`, `acks`, `decisions`), pinned by US-004 unit tests.
5. **Per-collapse log spam under high-volume noise** — if a member emits 500 duplicate `kind=done` reports in a sustained loop, the collapse pass would log 500 single-row groups, defeating the dedup goal. Mitigation: log line shape includes `count=<N>` so a single line per collapse group covers all N originals; the budget is O(distinct groups) not O(rows). Stderr is throttled by `warnThreshold`.
6. **Stderr surface differs slash-vs-CLI** — slash invocations don't surface stderr to the operator. Mitigation: the per-collapse `appendLog` line is the universal channel; stderr is the extra CLI-only signal. AGENTS.md and the CHANGELOG entry document this asymmetry.
7. **Plugin marketplace.json drift** — repo AGENTS.md flags this as a known repeat failure mode. Mitigation: US-010 lists all 6 version-bearing files explicitly; `scripts/bump-version.js 3.6.0` covers the 5 internal locations (per existing convention) plus the 3 codexu-side marketplace indexes manually.
8. **Submodule pointer-bump miss** — toolkit submodule edits require a two-commit flow per `codexu/AGENTS.md`. Mitigation: US-012 enumerates the codexu-side commit step explicitly.
9. **Disconfirming measurement under-shoots the brainstorm's "30% reduction" target** — preliminary 5/498 = 1% reduction. Mitigation: US-001's measurement is the gate; if measured reduction stays below 5% after running against the actual implementation, US-001 escalates with `kind=question` for operator triage before US-002+ ships.
10. **Test-suite Windows wall-time creep** — current target is < 60s default-concurrency. New tests should not require denylist entries unless they exercise process/lock timing. Mitigation: US-004/US-005/US-006/US-008 tests are all pure-function or fixture-based; estimate total added test time < 3s.
11. **Concurrent review-mail invocations across crews** — there is no global cross-crew lock. The collapse pass is per-invocation in-process, so concurrent invocations cannot race each other; the only durable mutation is `manifest.lastReviewedSeq` which is already inside `withManifestLock`. No additional locking needed.

## Acceptance Criteria

(Copied verbatim from `selected-direction.md § Criteria`, with planner clarifications applied per Phase 4 multi-model review):

1. **(F-002 split into AC1a and AC1b)**
   - **AC1a [CLI]**: A `node tools/crews.js review-mail <name> --crew <crew> --cwd <ws>` invocation against a mailbox containing 3+ consecutive identical `(sender, kind=done, body-hash, summary)` rows with empty `replyTo` / `payload.replyTo` / `payload.replyToId` / `acks` / `decisions` emits exactly one collapsed row with `collapsedCount=N`, exactly one stderr warning line (because `args.output === 'cli'` AND `count >= warnThreshold`), and exactly one `appendLog` line per collapse group in `crews.log`.
   - **AC1b [Slash]**: The same scenario invoked via `/crews:review-mail` emits exactly one collapsed row with `collapsedCount=N` and exactly one `appendLog` line per collapse group in `crews.log`, but NO stderr output (because `args.output === 'slash'`). The slash-vs-CLI stderr asymmetry is intentional and documented in AGENTS.md (US-011).
2. A `/crews:review-mail` invocation against rows that have ANY differing `replyTo`, `acks`, `decisions`, `kind`, or body-hash returns each row individually (zero collapse) — verified via fuzz over the existing local sample corpus AND a targeted unit test.
3. The post-collapse review cursor (`lastReviewedSeq`) is identical to the cursor that would have advanced under the pre-collapse behavior — `tests/strict-ack-review-mail.test.js` must continue passing without modification of its assertions about cursor position.
4. **(F-010 specified boundary)** Setting `CREWS_REVIEW_MAIL_COLLAPSE=off` produces all of: (a) JSON stdout byte-for-byte identical to pre-3.6.0 behavior INCLUDING key order and absence of `collapsedCount/collapsedSeqs/collapsedIds` from every entry, (b) zero stderr output (no warnings written), (c) zero new `review-mail collapse:` lines appended to `crews.log` during the invocation, (d) `manifest.lastReviewedSeq` and `lastReviewedAt` advance to byte-identical values as collapse-enabled mode would have. US-007 regression test asserts all four conditions explicitly.
5. **(F-001 rewritten as decision gate)** US-001 produces a measurement report at `.ralph/jobs/crews-redundant-empty-kind-tag-emissions/offline-measurement-report.md` with: `total_rows`, `collapsed_groups`, `extra_dups_eliminated`, `percent_reduction`, per-member breakdown, and 5 sample collapsed groups. The measurement INDEPENDENTLY asserts `zero rows with non-empty (replyTo OR payload.replyTo OR payload.replyToId OR non-empty acks OR non-empty decisions) get coalesced` (this is the safety floor — must always hold; failure here halts the job). The `percent_reduction` value is reported but is NOT itself a pass/fail criterion. **Decision gate**: when `percent_reduction < 5%`, US-001 writes a clear `[GATE]` block to stdout and to `offline-measurement-report.md` surfacing 3 options to the operator (`(A) proceed as structural improvement + telemetry channel / (B) defer in favor of D-003/D-004 / (C) widen corpus to other crews`). The orchestrator emits a `kind=question` to the operator with these options and PAUSES execution of US-002+ until the operator decision is recorded. The brainstorm's original "≥ 30% reduction" target is preserved as the ASPIRATIONAL design hope, but is not a release gate — the real release gate is "operator decision recorded OR percent_reduction ≥ 5%."
6. A new `crews.log` line shape `review-mail collapse: name=<name> crew=<crew> kind=<k> count=<N> seqRange=<a>..<b> bodyHash=<prefix> version=<v> listenerExit=<reason> turnBoundaryCount=<N>` appears for every collapse pass and is grep-able for false-positive audit. (Extended with D-002 telemetry fields per US-009.)
7. The proactive-routing payload-batching path (`stop.js:1379-1418`) is explicitly checked for whether it can produce the same kind of duplicate at the `payload.entries[]` level. **VERIFIED**: `expandReviewRows` in `review-mail.js:121-135` flattens `payload.entries[]` into leaf rows BEFORE the collapse pass runs, so the leaf-row collapse pass naturally covers proactive batches. NO separate batch-level pass is added. US-009 verifies this with a fixture-based test asserting a proactive-batch row with 3 identical entries collapses to one row.
8. All existing crews tests pass; tests are added or modified only as follows: (a) NEW test files `tests/version-runtime.test.js`, `tests/collapse-key.test.js`, `tests/collapse-review-rows.test.js`; (b) MODIFIED `tests/review-mail-command.test.js` (additive: collapse-coverage cases appended; no existing-case assertions changed); (c) MODIFIED `tests/command-args-parity.test.js` (additive: stdout key-order pin at 191-196 extended to include collapsed fields in stable order — pre-3.6.0 keys preserved); (d) UNCHANGED `tests/strict-ack-review-mail.test.js` (serves as the cursor-regression anchor for US-006).

Plus planner-added ACs:

9. `lib/version.js::getPluginVersion()` reads `.claude-plugin/plugin.json::version` at runtime (NOT `package.json`; crews has none — see Scope > In Scope planner-clarification footer) and is used in the collapse log line. A unit test asserts the return value matches `.claude-plugin/plugin.json::version` after the version bump in US-010.
10. The empty-metadata predicate `isEmptyMetadata(row)` explicitly checks ALL five fields: top-level `replyTo`, `payload.replyTo`, `payload.replyToId`, `acks` (length > 0), `decisions` (length > 0). A unit test fails the predicate (returns `false`) for each field independently.
11. Plugin version is bumped via `node ai-developer-toolkit/plugins/crews/scripts/bump-version.js 3.6.0` which atomically updates 6 stamping locations (2 plugin manifests + 3 marketplace indexes + `tests/version.test.js`). The codexu-root `AGENTS.md` "Active plugin versions" table row is ALSO bumped manually (outside `bump-version.js` scope). US-010 verifies all 7 locations show `3.6.0`.
12. Full crews test suite passes in under 90s at default concurrency on Windows (the AGENTS.md "Test cadence" loosened ceiling for v1.5.2+); no new test enters the serial denylist.
13. **(F-006)** `collapsedIds[]` uses the leaf-id chain `row.reportId || row.outboxId || row.id` for each member, so a collapsed proactive-batch group exposes leaf-level drill-down (not just the parent inbox id). A unit test asserts the chain by seeding a proactive-batch row with 3 identical `payload.entries[]` and verifying `collapsedIds[]` carries the 3 distinct leaf `reportId` / `outboxId` values, not the shared parent inbox `id`.
14. **(F-007)** Collapse-coverage parity tests in `tests/command-args-parity.test.js` invoke the dispatcher form (`node tools/crews.js review-mail ...`), NEVER the deprecated wrapper (`node tools/review-mail.js ...`). This keeps stderr assertions clean (the deprecation shim emits its own stderr line that would intersect with collapse-warning assertions).

## Suggested Decomposition

Cluster definitions for parallel-vs-serial execution. Matches `suggested-decomposition.json` byte-for-byte at the cluster/dependency/risk level.

### Cluster: measurement-gate
- Stories: US-001
- Phase: 1
- Depends on: None
- File-overlap evidence: shared=[]; exclusive=[`.ralph/jobs/crews-redundant-empty-kind-tag-emissions/offline-measurement.mjs`, `.ralph/jobs/crews-redundant-empty-kind-tag-emissions/offline-measurement-report.md`]; risk=low
- `execution_mode` rationale: Pre-ship measurement script lives outside the crews plugin and gates whether subsequent clusters are worth running. No file overlap with code clusters, so it can run as Phase 1 standalone.

### Cluster: foundation-libs
- Stories: US-002, US-003
- Phase: 2
- Depends on: None
- File-overlap evidence: shared=[]; exclusive=[`ai-developer-toolkit/plugins/crews/lib/version.js`, `ai-developer-toolkit/plugins/crews/lib/collapse-key.js`, `ai-developer-toolkit/plugins/crews/tests/version-runtime.test.js`, `ai-developer-toolkit/plugins/crews/tests/collapse-key.test.js`]; risk=low
- `execution_mode` rationale: Two independent helper modules with disjoint files and disjoint tests. Can run in parallel with measurement-gate because neither touches `review-mail.js` or the same test file.

### Cluster: core-collapse
- Stories: US-004, US-005, US-006, US-007, US-008, US-009
- Phase: 3
- Depends on: foundation-libs
- File-overlap evidence: shared=[`ai-developer-toolkit/plugins/crews/hooks/commands/review-mail.js`, `ai-developer-toolkit/plugins/crews/lib/collapse-review-rows.js`, `ai-developer-toolkit/plugins/crews/tests/review-mail-command.test.js`, `ai-developer-toolkit/plugins/crews/tests/collapse-review-rows.test.js`, `ai-developer-toolkit/plugins/crews/tests/command-args-parity.test.js`]; exclusive=[]; risk=high
- `execution_mode` rationale: All six stories edit `review-mail.js` or the new collapse helper or its tests. Same-file edits across review-mail.js, command-args-parity.test.js, and the new collapse helper force serial execution; each story builds on the previous one logically (helper → wire-in → cursor regression → env-off bit-identical → stderr warning → telemetry).

### Cluster: ship-and-docs

- Phase: 4
- Depends on: core-collapse

## Open Questions

Carried forward from `selected-direction.md § Open questions to carry into planning`, with planner answers / impl-phase deferrals annotated:

1. **Should D-001 collapse be exact `(sender, kind, normalized body+summary+replyTo+ackSet hash)` only — refusing any near-similarity match in v1.x for safety?** Lens consensus: YES. Plan adopts: exact hash, no near-similarity. US-004 ACs lock this.

2. **Should collapsed rows expose `collapsedCount`, `collapsedSeqs`, and `collapsedIds` in the review-mail JSON output, accepting a documented output shape change?** Lens consensus: YES. Plan adopts: additive fields, single-row entries keep their existing shape (`collapsedCount` absent or equal to 1 — implementation TBD per US-005; recommendation is `collapsedCount` absent for non-collapsed rows to minimize shape change). `tests/command-args-parity.test.js:191-196` updated in same commit as wire-in. CHANGELOG documents.

3. **Is it acceptable that `outbox.jsonl` and `mailbox-history.jsonl` keep the duplicate audit rows while review-mail advances the cursor past all collapsed rows?** Lens consensus: YES. Plan adopts: durable audit log untouched; this is a load-bearing invariant of D-001 vs D-003.

4. **Does the collapse pass need to dedup across `payload.entries` batches in proactive-routing notifications (`stop.js:1379-1418`), or only at the leaf row level in `review-mail.js`?** Devil's Advocate flag. **Plan answer (verified by research)**: `expandReviewRows` in `review-mail.js:121-135` flattens `payload.entries[]` into leaf rows BEFORE the collapse pass runs, so the leaf-row collapse pass naturally covers proactive batches. NO separate batch-level pass needed. US-009 verifies this with a fixture-based test.

5. **For each duplicate observed in the original cases, was it (a) one assistant turn with multiple report tags, (b) multiple assistant turns, (c) a Stop retry, or (d) review-mail expansion of one `payload.entries` batch? — D-002 telemetry will answer; D-001 collapse rules must remain safe under all four.** Deferred to impl: US-009's D-002 telemetry bundle adds the `listenerExit=<reason>` and `turnBoundaryCount=<N>` fields to the per-collapse log line, so the operator can classify by mechanism post-ship. The collapse rule itself (consecutive same-key, empty metadata) is structurally safe under all four mechanisms because the audit log is untouched.

6. **Should `kind=done` be modeled as a terminal state transition after which idle member turns are no-op until new lead mail (D-004's framing), or as a repeatable per-turn report?** Deferred per Out-of-Scope; D-001 doesn't address this.

7. **Which exact crews versions produced Case A (codexu v5.50 impl member) and Case B (seval-540475 summarizer-behavior member)?** Carried into US-009 telemetry as part of the `version=<v>` field in the collapse log line. Plan-phase note: research confirmed deployed crews is v3.5.0, NOT the brainstorm's v1.x framing — the line refs are still accurate but the version semantics differ.

Planner-added open questions:

8. **Disconfirming measurement — is 1% reduction enough to ship D-001?** Preliminary measurement found 5 extra-dups in 498 mailbox-history rows on the local corpus. The brainstorm's "≥ 30% reduction" target appears unreachable on this corpus. US-001 re-measures with the actual implementation's collapse logic; if result stays below 5%, US-001 escalates `kind=question` to the operator before US-002+ ships. The fall-back framing is "ship as structural improvement + telemetry channel; the D-002 bundled telemetry is itself the primary value, not the collapse ratio." Operator decision: ship anyway, or pivot.

9. **Should single-row entries omit `collapsedCount` entirely or include `collapsedCount: 1`?** Plan recommendation: omit, to minimize JSON-shape change. Impl-phase confirms with `command-args-parity.test.js` ergonomics. Deferred to US-005.

10. **Should `bodyHash` be sha256 hex prefix (e.g. first 12 chars) or full hash in the log line?** Plan recommendation: 12-char prefix for log-line readability; full hash for the internal collapse key. Deferred to US-003.

11. **stderr warning threshold tuning**: default `warnThreshold=3` per brainstorm. Should this be relaxed (e.g. 5) if the offline measurement shows even small N-runs are common-and-expected? Deferred to US-008 + US-001 reading.
